title: Explore Adipose Tissue Biology
bodyHtml:
Explore Adipose Tissue Biology
Adipose tissue plays a key role in metabolism and disease. Whether you're interested in gene regulation, cell type composition, or clinical associations, these two open-access portals provide rich, complementary datasets and tools to support discovery in adipose biology.
Search above to see results for your gene of interest from either portal.
Below you can see samples of the kind of results you can expect to see on each portal.
Mammalian Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (MATKP)
The Mammalian Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (MATKP) is a developing open community resource for multi-species mammalian adipose biology. Initial features include harmonized transcriptomic datasets from human and mouse tissues, human genetic data, and adipose-relevant genomic annotations. MATKP is produced by a multidisciplinary US-based team of researchers and clinicians from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Evan Rosen and Linus Tsai), the University of Chicago (Margo Emont), and the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard (Melina Claussnitzer, Orr Ashenberg, Noël Burtt, and Jason Flannick). MATKP is funded by the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (RC2 DK116691).

Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (ATKP)
The Adipose Tissue Knowledge Portal (ATKP) is an open resource that makes human adipose data available to the scientific community. ATKP emphasizes human clinical relevance by integrating transcriptomic and proteomic data across >6,000 individuals, various fat depots, and in vitro perturbation studies. ATKP is developed and maintained by a European-based team of researchers and clinicians from the Karolinska Institutet and Helmholtz Munich (Mikael Ryden, Niklas Mejhert, Lucas Massier).
